name: Do you need a permit to add a bathroom in Los Angeles County?

mainEntity.name: Which parts of a bathroom addition require permits in Los Angeles-area cities?
mainEntity.text: Which parts of a bathroom addition require permits in Los Angeles-area cities?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most bathroom additions in Los Angeles-area cities require permits because they usually involve plumbing, electrical, ventilation, and sometimes framing changes. If the project only includes cosmetic updates like paint, tile, or replacing a vanity in the same location, it may not need a permit. But the moment you move a drain, add a new light circuit, install a fan, open a wall, or change the structure, permitting typically applies. For homeowners, this matters because a bathroom addition often combines several trades, and even one unpermitted component can create problems during inspection or resale. Before starting, it is smart to confirm the permit path with the local building department and have plans that show fixture layout, electrical, ventilation, and any structural modifications. That avoids delays, corrections, and expensive rework later.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes. A bathroom addition typically needs permits for plumbing, electrical, mechanical, and any structural work. Cosmetic-only work, such as painting or replacing finishes in the same locations, may be permit-exempt. Moving drains, adding circuits, removing walls, or changing ventilation usually triggers review.
